en: Vibhaṅga:
Analysis of the Training Rules 1.
Exposition according to the Abhidhamma (Abhidhammabhājanīya)
The five training rules:
the training rule of abstaining from taking life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct,
the training rule of abstaining from false speech, and [abstaining from] fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
The training precept of abstention from taking life. In this context, what is the training precept of abstention from taking life?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge...
For one who abstains from the destruction of life, whatever at that time is the refraining, the desisting, the turning away from,
the abstinence from, the non-doing, the non-performing, the non-transgression, the not overstepping the limit, and the demolition of the bridge regarding the destruction of life—
this is called the training precept of abstinence from the destruction of life.
The remaining factors are associated with abstinence.
Therein, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who is abstaining from taking life—the volition, the act of intending, and the state of having intended at that time—[this is the training precept of abstaining from taking life].
This is called "the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
The remaining factors are associated with volition (*cetanā*).
In that regard, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one who abstains from taking life—at that time, whatever contact there is, ... [and so on] ...
whatever exertion and non-distraction there is—this is called the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?
At whatever time a wholesome consciousness belonging to the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by joy,
dissociated from knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by joy,
dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge,
with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge … [and so on].
When one refrains from taking life with a state accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort—

at that time, whatever abstention, desisting, refraining, abstinence, non-doing, non-making, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and destruction of the bridge regarding the taking of life— this is [right action].
This is called "the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
The remaining factors are associated with that abstention.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort, for one who abstains from the destruction of life— at that time, whatever volition, intention, and state of intending there is—
this is called the training precept of abstaining from the destruction of life.
All remaining phenomena are associated with that volition.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort, for one who refrains from taking life—contact ... [and so on] ... exertion, non-distraction:
this is called "the training precept of abstaining from taking life."
Therein, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking what is not given?
…pe… the training precept of abstaining from sexual misconduct?
…pe… the training precept of abstaining from false speech? …pe…
What is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness?

It is, at whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen—accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge—for one who is refraining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness;
at that time, [the volition] regarding fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness...
Abstaining, desisting, refraining, abstinence, non-action, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the bridge—
this is called the training precept of abstaining from fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants, which are the basis for negligence.
All remaining phenomena are associated with this abstinence.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that cause negligence? It is,

at whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge for one who is abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that cause negligence—
the volition, the act of willing, and the state of having willed at that time.
This is called the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that are the basis for negligence.
The remaining phenomena are associated with volition.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants that are the basis for negligence?

At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge, for one abstaining from the occasion of negligence consisting in fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants—at that time, whatever contact...

[and so on] ...whatever exertion and non-distraction there is—this is called the training precept of abstaining from the occasion of negligence consisting in fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from the occasion of negligence consisting in fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants?

At whatever time a wholesome state of consciousness belonging to the sense sphere has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, and with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by joy,
dissociated from knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by joy,
dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort … [and so on].

Accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity and associated with knowledge with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge … [and so on].
When one abstains from the basis for negligence consisting of fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort—

at that time, whatever refraining, desisting, turning away, abstinence, non-doing, non-performance, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and destruction of the bridge there is in relation to the basis for negligence consisting of fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants— this is [right action].
This is called "the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
All remaining phenomena are associated with this abstention.
In that regard, what is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge, and with volitional effort,
in one who is abstaining from the occasion of negligence consisting in fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants— at that time, whatever volition, intention, and state of intending there is—
this is called the training precept of abstention from the occasion of negligence consisting in fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants.
The remaining factors are associated with volition.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by equanimity and dissociated from knowledge...

For one who abstains from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence with volitional effort, whatever at that time is contact … [and so on] … exertion, non-distraction—
this is called the training rule of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
There are five training rules.
The training precept of abstaining from taking life, the training precept of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training precept of abstaining from sexual misconduct,
the training precept of abstaining from false speech, and the training precept of abstaining from fermented and distilled liquors that cause heedlessness.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

It is when a wholesome state of consciousness belonging to the sense sphere has arisen—accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, whether inferior, intermediate, or superior; dominated by desire, dominated by energy, or dominated by mind.
… [the state] dominated by investigation … dominated by desire, whether inferior, middling, or superior … dominated by energy,
whether inferior, middling, or superior … dominated by mind, whether inferior, middling, or superior … dominated by investigation,
whether inferior, middling, or superior, for one who abstains from taking life— at that time, whatever [state] there is regarding the abstention from taking life...
Abstaining, desisting, refraining, abstinence, non-action, non-doing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the bridge—
this is called the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
All remaining phenomena are associated with this abstinence.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?

It is when a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, whether it be inferior, middling, or superior; or where desire is predominant, or energy is predominant, or mind is predominant.

… [the state] dominated by investigation … dominated by desire … inferior … middling … superior … dominated by energy … inferior … middling … superior … dominated by mind … inferior … middling … superior … dominated by investigation,
for one who abstains from taking life— at that time, whatever volition, intentionality, and state of having intended there is— this is [wholesome volitional action].
This is called "the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
The remaining factors are associated with volition (*cetanā*).
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge—whether it be inferior, middling, or superior;

whether it be dominated by desire, dominated by energy, dominated by consciousness, or dominated by investigation; whether it be dominated by desire and be inferior, middling, or superior; or whether it be dominated by energy... [and so forth].
Whether it be inferior, middling, or superior; whether dominated by mind, inferior, middling, or superior;

or dominated by investigation, inferior, middling, or superior—for one who abstains from the destruction of life, whatever at that time is contact … [and so on] … exertion and non-distraction—this is called the training precept of abstaining from the destruction of life.
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking life?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge,
and with volitional effort … [and so on] … or accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge … [and so on].
Accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge … [as above] … accompanied by equanimity,

dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort: inferior … medium … superior … dominated by desire … dominated by energy … dominated by consciousness … dominated by desire, inferior … medium … superior.
… whether dominated by energy that is inferior, middling, or superior; or dominated by mind that is inferior,
middling, or superior— in one who abstains from the destruction of life, whatever at that time is the desisting, the refraining, the turning away from,

the abstinence from, the non-doing, the non-making, the non-transgression, the not overstepping the limit, and the destruction of the bridge regarding the destruction of life— this is [the virtue of restraint].
This is called “the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
The remaining states are associated with abstention … [and so on] … the remaining states are associated with volition … [and so on].
Contact … [and so on] … exertion and non-distraction—this is called the training precept of abstaining from taking life.
In this regard, what is the training precept of abstaining from taking what is not given? … [and so on] …

The training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct …pe… the training rule of abstaining from false speech …pe… the training rule of abstaining from fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy and associated with knowledge—whether it be inferior, middling, or superior;

whether it has zeal as its dominant factor, energy as its dominant factor, consciousness as its dominant factor, or investigation as its dominant factor; whether it has zeal as its dominant factor and is inferior, middling, or superior; or has energy as its dominant factor... [and so on].
Whether it be inferior, middling, or superior; whether it be dominated by mind, inferior, middling, or superior;

or whether it be dominated by investigation, inferior, middling, or superior—the abstention, desisting, refraining, abstinence, non-doing, non-performing, and non-transgression at that time of one who abstains from the use of fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
Not transgressing the limit and destroying the bridge—this is called the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, distilled spirits, and intoxicants that cause heedlessness.
All remaining phenomena are associated with this abstinence... [and so forth].
The remaining states associated with volition—
namely, contact … pe … exertion and non-distraction—
this is called “the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.”
In this context, what is the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence?
At whatever time wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge,
and with volitional effort … [or] accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge … [and so forth].
Accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge … [as above] … accompanied by equanimity,

dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort: inferior … middling … superior … dominated by desire … dominated by energy … dominated by consciousness … dominated by desire, inferior … middling … superior.
… the inferior, middling, or superior predominance of energy … the inferior, middling,

or superior predominance of mind … for one abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence— at that time, whatever refraining, desisting, abstaining, abstinence, non-doing, non-performing, non-transgression, not overstepping the limit, and destruction of the bridge [constitutes] the abstention from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
This is called the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, distilled spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
The remaining phenomena are associated with abstention … [as above] … the remaining phenomena are associated with volition … [as above].
Contact … [and so on] … exertion, non-distraction—
this is called the training precept of abstaining from fermented liquor, spirits, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
What phenomena are the trainings?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen, accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge, having as its object a visible form … pe … or a mental phenomenon,
or whatever [object] it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction.
These states are the trainings.
What are the states that are trainings?
At whatever time a wholesome sense-sphere consciousness has arisen that is accompanied by joy, associated with knowledge,
and with volitional effort … [and] accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge … [and so forth].
Accompanied by joy, dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge … [and so on] … accompanied by equanimity,
associated with knowledge, with volitional effort … [and so on].
Accompanied by equanimity, dissociated from knowledge …pe… accompanied by equanimity,
dissociated from knowledge, with volitional effort, having visible form as its object …pe… or having mental phenomena as its object,
or whatever else it may be directed toward— at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction.
These are the states that are trainings. What states are trainings?
At whatever time one develops the path for rebirth in the form realm …pe… [as above] … these are the states that are trainings.

He develops the path for rebirth in the formless realm …pe… he develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the diminution [of defilements], for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage;
secluded from sensual pleasures …pe… he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice.
At that time there is sluggish direct knowledge; there is contact ... [and so on] ... there is non-distraction.
These states are the trainings.
This is the *Abhidhamma-bhājaniya*.
2. Interrogation on Questions.
Five training rules:
the training rule of abstaining from taking life, the training rule of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training rule of abstaining from sexual misconduct...

The training precept of abstaining from taking what is not given, the training precept of abstaining from false speech, and the training precept of abstaining from fermented and distilled liquors and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence.
Of these five training precepts, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, and how many are indeterminate? …pe… How many are with conflict, and how many are without conflict?
2.1. The Triplet:
Only wholesome.
It may be associated with pleasant feeling; it may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
States that are subject to ripening.
Not acquired by clinging, yet conducive to clinging.
Not defiled, yet subject to defilement.
They are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.
They may be accompanied by rapture, they may be accompanied by pleasure, or they may be accompanied by equanimity.
They are not to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation.
Those whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation;
they lead to accumulation;
they are neither for those in training nor for those beyond training.
Limited.
Having a limited object.
Intermediate.
The indeterminate states.
They should not be said to have the Path as their object, nor to have the Path as their cause, nor to have the Path as their predominance.
They may be arisen, or they may be unarisen; they should not be said to be bound to arise.
It may be past, it may be future, or it may be present.
Its object is present.
It may be internal, it may be external, or it may be both internal and external.
Having external objects.
Non-manifesting and non-reacting.
2.2.1. Group on Causes (Hetugocchaka) They are not causes, but they possess causes; they are associated with causes.

They should not be described as "both causes and possessing causes," but rather as "possessing causes but not being causes. They should not be described as "both causes and associated with causes," but rather as "associated with causes but not being causes. They are neither causes nor do they possess causes.
2.2.2. The Minor Intermediate Dyads (Cūḷantaraduka) With conditions;
conditioned; non-demonstrable; non-reacting; immaterial; mundane; cognizable by something; not cognizable by something. 2.2.3.
The Group on Taints (Āsavagocchaka)
The taints (āsava) are neither "taints and associated with taints" nor can they be said to be "both taints and associated with taints";

rather, they are associated with taints but are not themselves taints. Those things that are associated with taints but are not themselves taints are dissociated from the taints and are associated with taints.
14.2.2.4. The Group on Fetters, etc.
There are no fetters … pe … there are no ties … pe …
...no floods ...pe...
no yokes ...pe...
no hindrances ...pe...
No perversions … [as above] … 2.2.10. Mahantaraduka:
With objects, not consciousness, mental factors, associated with consciousness, conjoined with consciousness, generated by consciousness.

Co-existent with consciousness, following after consciousness, conjoined with and produced by consciousness, co-existent with that which is conjoined with and produced by consciousness, following after that which is conjoined with and produced by consciousness, external, not derived from the primary elements, and not clung-to.
14.2.2.11. The Group on Clinging (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.
There is no clinging …pe… there are no defilements …pe… they are not to be abandoned by vision,
not to be abandoned by cultivation, and they do not have as their cause that which is to be abandoned by vision.
They have roots to be abandoned by cultivation; they are accompanied by initial application and sustained application;
they may be with rapture, or without rapture; they may be accompanied by rapture, or not accompanied by rapture; they may be accompanied by pleasure, or not accompanied by pleasure;
they may be accompanied by equanimity, or not accompanied by equanimity; they belong to the sense sphere, not to the fine-material sphere, and not to the immaterial sphere.
Included, not leading to liberation, indeterminate, surpassable, and with conflict.
The interrogation on questions is finished. The Analysis of the Training Precepts (Sikkhāpada-vibhaṅga) is concluded.
